summary: A kilo of carrots, parsnips and swede roasted in one tin with new potatoes and whole garlic cloves, then dressed with the softened garlic, lemon and parsley and finished with feta and nuts. The simplest record in this set: one tin, one 50-minute roast, and a dressing stirred together at the end.

ingredients.item: Mixed root vegetables — carrots, parsnips, swede — cut into batons and halved

ingredients.note: Tree nuts and/or peanuts unless you choose a seed-only pack.

ingredients.quantity: The source seasons the tin to taste and gives no weight.

method.instruction: Heat the oven to 200°C conventional, or 180°C fan. The source prints gas mark 5 alongside those figures; all three are recorded as written and none is a conversion made here.
Put the prepared roots, new potatoes and whole garlic cloves into a large roasting tin and tuck the rosemary and thyme sprigs among them.
Drizzle over 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, toss until everything is evenly coated, and season.
Roast for 50 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Squeeze the softened garlic out of its skin and combine it with the lemon juice, chopped parsley and the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil, either blended or whisked in a bowl.
Pour the dressing over the roasted vegetables and toss, then scatter the nuts and crumbled feta over the top to serve.

yield_note: Serves 4, as stated by the source. Source times: 50 minutes roasting within 65 minutes in total, with no separate preparation time listed. The source gives no resting time, and none is invented here.

caveats: No meat, poultry or fish is involved, so no internal-temperature threshold applies. The endpoint is texture: the roots should be tender after the 50-minute roast.
Allergens: milk in the feta, and nuts in the topping. A mixed snacking pack may contain peanuts as well as tree nuts; a seed-only pack avoids both.
Whole garlic cloves roast in their skins and come out very hot; let them cool before squeezing them out.
